cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Build a Coalition
cards.instruction: Recruit someone to your side so your position appears broader and more legitimate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Sit with me for the allotment shed vote. It shouldn't look like just my project.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I only support it if everyone gets a key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Shared keys. Agreed. Will you join me now?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The new plot holders need to hear that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring them over. We can present it together as the shared-access proposal.

mechanism: A grants a shared-access concession while recruiting visible allies, keeping personal direction over a proposal made to appear broader.
confusable: D52 seeks endorsement; D55 builds a group whose breadth lends legitimacy, so B must help recruit or represent more than one supporter.
comparison: An allotment shed coalition forms around shared keys, while the pottery alternative adds weekend users to a late-hours request.
seedUse: Use D55-a key condition and new plot holders, with S01 approval defining the concession and who may present it.
